records.title: Automatic Emergency Braking / Forward Collision Phantom Activation
records.description: Third-generation Muranos with Nissan's Forward Emergency Braking (FEB)/Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) have widely reported 'phantom braking' — the system suddenly and forcefully brakes when no obstacle is present, creating rear-end collision and loss-of-control risk. The problem is associated with the front grille radar/sensor module (Bosch-supplied) misreading the road. The Murano is named in AEB class-action litigation alongside other Nissan models, and Nissan issued TSBs addressing false AEB/FCW activation on 2019-2024 Murano (Z52).
records.solution: Dealer diagnosis per the applicable TSB; remedies have included radar sensor recalibration, software/ECU reprogramming, or sensor replacement. Keep the front emblem/grille radar area clean and free of obstructions (snow, mud, badges). The FEB system can be temporarily disabled via the vehicle settings menu while driving in conditions that trigger false activation.

records.title: Battery Drain and No-Start from Telematics/Infotainment Modules Staying Awake
records.description: A recurring owner complaint on newer Nissan crossovers, including Murano, is a dead battery after sitting overnight or for a few days despite the battery testing good initially. Reports often point to parasitic draw from telematics, AV control, or body control modules that fail to enter sleep mode, sometimes accompanied by app connectivity glitches or infotainment oddities. The issue can be intermittent, making it difficult to catch unless a proper draw test is performed after module timeout.
records.solution: Start with battery state-of-health and charging-system checks, then perform a parasitic draw test with the vehicle fully asleep. If draw remains excessive, isolate the circuit by pulling fuses and checking telematics, AV, and BCM-related branches; software updates, module resets, or replacement of the offending module may be required. Replacing the battery alone often provides only temporary relief if the root draw remains.

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for a true parasitic draw test after all modules time out; many quick battery tests miss the actual problem.
If the vehicle sits for long periods, a smart maintainer can prevent deep discharge while diagnosis is pending.

records.title: Front Driver Seat Frame/Track Looseness Causing Rocking, Clicking, or Unintended Movement
records.description: Owners have reported the driver's seat rocking front-to-back, clicking during braking/acceleration, or feeling loose on its track. Nissan has issued service information on seat track/frame-related movement complaints on late-model vehicles, and owner reports indicate the issue can appear at relatively low mileage. The problem is usually caused by play in the seat track assembly, frame hardware, or worn internal seat adjuster components rather than the floor mounting points themselves.
records.solution: Road-test the vehicle and confirm whether the movement occurs during throttle tip-in, braking, or over bumps. Inspect seat track bolts, rail alignment, and the seat adjuster assembly; repairs typically involve tightening hardware to spec, replacing the seat track/adjuster assembly, or replacing the seat frame if internal play is present. If the seat has power functions, verify all positions after repair and recalibrate memory settings if equipped.

communityRecommendations.content: Have the dealer verify torque on seat mounting fasteners before replacing expensive seat components.
Document exactly when the seat moves—braking, acceleration, or cornering—to help isolate track vs. frame play.

records.title: Front Radar/Sensor Malfunctions Triggering AEB, ICC, and Forward Collision Warnings
records.description: Owners have reported intermittent 'Front radar unavailable,' AEB/FCW warnings, disabled intelligent cruise control, and related driver-assistance faults on 2021-2024 Murano models. In many cases the system disables itself in rain, road spray, or after minor front-end impacts, but some complaints describe repeated warnings in normal conditions due to sensor alignment, bracket movement, contamination, or radar unit faults. Because these systems are tied to emergency braking and adaptive cruise functions, repeated failures are a significant safety concern.
records.solution: Scan all ADAS modules for stored faults and inspect the front radar sensor area for damage, contamination, or mounting/bracket misalignment. Nissan service procedures typically require radar aiming/calibration after bumper work or sensor replacement; if warnings persist, the radar sensor, harness, or bracket may need replacement followed by static/dynamic calibration. Also verify battery voltage and CAN communication health, since low voltage can trigger cascading ADAS faults.

communityRecommendations.content: Do not replace the radar blindly; first inspect the emblem area, bracket, and bumper fitment, then perform proper calibration.
Keep photos of warning messages and note weather conditions, since intermittent ADAS faults are often hard to duplicate.

records.title: Rearview Camera Image Blank, Distorted, or Intermittent Due to AV Control Unit/Camera Fault
records.description: Multiple Murano owners in the 2021-2024 range have reported the backup camera showing a black screen, frozen image, blue screen, or distorted picture when shifting into reverse. This is also covered by Nissan/NHTSA recall actions affecting rearview camera display reliability on Nissan vehicles, including Murano, because the image may not display as required by FMVSS 111. Owners typically experience intermittent failure at first, then more frequent loss of image, especially after startup or in hot/cold weather.
records.solution: Confirm the concern by repeatedly cycling ignition and selecting reverse while monitoring the display. Diagnosis usually involves checking for AV control unit software/hardware faults, camera harness connection issues, and camera module failure; Nissan recall/TSB procedures generally call for software update, AV control unit reprogramming, or replacement of the camera/control unit if the image remains unstable. If the vehicle is covered by an open recall, the recall remedy should be completed before paid repairs.

communityRecommendations.content: Check for open recalls by VIN before replacing the camera or display parts out of pocket.
If intermittent, record a video of the failed camera display to help the dealer reproduce the issue.

records.title: Sunroof Drain or Roof Area Water Intrusion Causing Wet Headliner/Carpet and Electrical Issues
records.description: Murano owners continue to report water leaks into the cabin, often showing up as damp headliner edges, wet front footwells, musty odor, or water near A-pillars after rain or car washes. The most common causes are restricted sunroof drains, disconnected drain tubes, or seal/body seam issues around the roof opening area. If ignored, the leak can damage carpet padding, connectors, and interior electronics.
records.solution: Water-test the roof and windshield perimeter while inspecting the sunroof cassette drains and A-pillar drain routing. Clear clogged drains with low-pressure air or line, repair or reconnect drain tubes, and inspect for seal or seam leaks if drains flow normally. Dry the carpet and underlayment thoroughly afterward to prevent mold and corrosion in connectors under the carpet.

communityRecommendations.content: Use only low-pressure air or flexible trimmer line to clear drains; high pressure can disconnect the drain tube.
After fixing the leak, lift and dry the carpet padding fully—surface drying alone often leaves odor and corrosion behind.
